 Bailey Pemberton Tue, October 27, 2026 at 8:19 PM EDT 4 min read CE.MI +1.78% 
 Credito Emiliano has delivered a powerful share price run in recent years, which puts fresh focus on whether the business is earning enough on its capital to warrant where the stock trades today. With the Excess Returns intrinsic value framework pointing squarely at the profits Credito Emiliano generates relative to its equity base, the question is how comfortably those returns line up with the current market price. 
 Over the past 5 years, Credito Emiliano has returned about 297.2%, so anyone looking at the stock now has to ask whether the returns the bank earns on its capital can support that kind of share price journey. 
 The business model depends heavily on how efficiently it turns its balance sheet into profit, which can shape expectations for future reinvestment needs and the pace at which any excess capital might build up over time. 
 Prefer to judge Credito Emiliano on earnings? See what Credito Emiliano's 12.1x P/E says about the price . 
 The issue now is whether Credito Emiliano's current share price fairly reflects the returns it earns on its capital when viewed through that Excess Returns lens. 
 For more context on whether Credito Emiliano's five year run lines up with the returns it earns on its capital, you can also start with a focused stock screen such as 195 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Does Credito Emiliano Look Fairly Valued on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit Credito Emiliano can generate over and above the return that equity investors require. On the inputs here, the bank is assumed to earn an average Return on Equity of 11.41%, with a Stable EPS of €1.75 per share and a Book Value of €13.89 per share that edges up to a Stable Book Value of €15.38 per share over time. Against a Cost of Equity of €1.53 per share, that leaves an estimated Excess Return of €0.22 per share, which is modest but positive. 
 On the income side, the dividend stream matters too. The Dividend Discount Model uses a current dividend of €0.85 per share, a payout ratio of 35.71% and a growth rate for those payouts capped at 3.44%. Taken together, these Excess Returns and dividend assumptions suggest the current €20.00 share price is broadly in line with what the model implies, so the current market tag already bakes in a fair amount of the expected profitability and capital growth story.
